provenance.notes: Masked decode with a long key/value context; a rank-2 all-zero additive mask broadcasts across query heads.
Offsetting V around 1.0 keeps the 1,024-key average away from zero, making scale errors in the per-split denominators and cross-split merge observable on masked decode split-K.
Boolean rank-4 broadcast-mask parity for masked split-K decode; includes both attended and masked keys.
A boolean mask over the key sequence is false for the first two heads and true for the other two. Fully masked heads must produce zero rows while the open heads retain their attention results.

Offsetting V to oscillate about 1.0 makes an accidental mean-of-V fallback an O(1) error while the required zero rows of the two fully masked heads stay exactly zero. This prevents the split-K zero-denominator guard from passing only because a zero-mean V fixture nearly cancels.

Logical-bool mask on the short-query split-K arm, false for the first half of the query rows and true for the rest. Its per-query mask rows use a different index path from decode, so a masked row must still carry zero probability mass through every split while its neighbours in the same tile keep their answers.

Logical-bool mask on the masked clustered split-key/value tile (sixteen queries over 1024 keys at head dim 128), false for the first eight query rows. Every split of a masked row carries zero mass and the merge emits a zero row, beside open rows of the same tile that must not be zeroed with it.
F16 short-query and rank-3 broadcast-mask parity for the masked split-K family.

Sixteen masked queries over 1024 keys at head dim 128 take the masked clustered split-key/value tile (the per-query split-K route keeps rank-3 masks and up to sixteen queries elsewhere); rank-2 additive mask.
Sixteen queries with a rank-4 logical-bool mask on the masked clustered split-key/value tile: rejected keys carry no mass across the split merge.
Sixteen f16 queries with a rank-2 additive mask on the masked clustered split-key/value tile.

Offsetting V around 1.0 makes normalization errors observable in masked short-query split-K with a rank-3 broadcast mask, including the per-split maximum and denominator that incorporate the additive mask.
Masked short-query attention with a long key/value context and an additive mask.
A query length of 17 lies outside the masked short-query split-K range and exercises the general masked attention path.
Rank-four float16 attention with 1 query head and 1 key/value head, key/query head width 16 and value head width 320.
Compact correctness case for the all-feature rank-4 tiled path.
Four heads with 32 queries and head dimension 32 check a short-query attention shape.
Head dimension 60 exercises the direct flash range for a realistic hidden size of 960.
A short-prompt GQA shape with 16 queries checks grouped heads and per-query output.

skipGpu.reason: Portable WGSL floating-point semantics do not guarantee preservation of the subnormal values required by this fixture. Backend evidence: Metal flushes denormals to zero in the ALU; the softmax exp/normalize and value-weighting produce subnormal probabilities that flush on GPU. Permanent FTZ limitation.

provenance.notes: A large but finite score gap leaves a valid subnormal softmax tail; multiplying that tail by a large finite V turns it into an ordinary output contribution.
Small rank-3 packed-head MHA fixture using ORT's q_num_heads/kv_num_heads layout convention.
Compact rank-3 GQA fixture: four packed query heads share two packed K/V heads.
Raw logits [0.5, 2.0] are tanh-softcapped before softmax, so ignoring softcap changes the output.
Compact ordering guard: two unmasked logits are softcapped before softmax, while a -inf-masked poison value must contribute zero.

Q, K and V are onnxruntime's Attention4DAttnMaskBoolAllFalse tensors; the mask is false across the first query row and true across the second, so the fully masked row must emit zero while the open row keeps its softmax answer — a whole-output zero is then a visible failure rather than the expected value.
Uses the official rank-4 Q/K/V shape and the standard [B, 1, Q, K] additive mask, which broadcasts across query heads.
Uses the official rank-4 Q/K/V shape with V head size 10 and the standard [Q, K] additive mask broadcast across batch and heads.
Uses the official rank-4 shape and scale attribute with deterministic generated data.
Uses the official rank-4 fp16 shape with deterministic generated data.
The f32 Q32 broadcast specialization maps 32 vec4 head segments to a fixed 32-lane subgroup, exercising one segment per lane with a complete head.
Covers standard additive-mask broadcasting from [Q, K] to [B, QH, Q, K].
Covers standard singleton-head additive-mask broadcasting from [B, 1, Q, K] to [B, QH, Q, K].
Rank-four float32 attention with 4 heads, head width 32, a 64-token sequence, and a boolean attention mask that cycles true/true/false/true across keys.

Rank-four float32 attention, 4 heads, head width 32, 64-token sequence. The first half of the query rows are masked out entirely and must produce zero rather than a divide-by-zero softmax denominator, while the second half keeps its normal result.

Rank-four float16 attention (8 heads, head width 64, 128-token sequence) with a boolean attention mask, which stays dtype-independent while a float mask would need to match Q/K/V's dtype. V is offset by 1.0 so the output stays near O(1) and float16 tolerance can catch a large normalization error.
Offsetting V around 1.0 makes normalization errors observable in masked float16 flash-cluster attention at headDim=64, including errors that preserve relative weights but change their sum.

Compact Attention-24 upper-left causal witness for qSeq=1 and kvSeq=4. The sole query may attend only the first key, so the output equals the first value rather than an average that includes future keys.
A rank-3 [batch, query, key] additive mask broadcasts across heads without a cache input.
A rank-3 [1, query, key] additive mask over rank-4 attention inputs checks broadcasting across batch and heads.

Query and key amplitudes put the raw scores well past the softcap, so the tanh clamp is the thing under test rather than a near-linear pass-through. The tolerance bounds the f32 tanh rounding difference.
Offsetting V around 1.0 keeps the 1,024-key average away from zero, exposing normalization errors when softcapped decode split-K merges partials with separate running maxima and denominators.
Offsetting V around 1.0 makes normalization and query-by-split indexing errors observable in short-query split-K GQA at q64/kv1024.
Amplitudes give the answer a magnitude of its own instead of a near-cancelling mean of V, which is what lets a tolerance this tight see a per-position error at f16.
Offsetting V around 1.0 keeps the 128-key average away from zero, exposing normalization errors in noncausal float16 GQA prefill at headDim=128 on both subgroup and reduced tiers.
Head width 96 with eight heads and 128 tokens; offset V near 1.0 keeps the noncausal float16 output away from zero so normalization errors remain observable.

Softcap-sensitive rank-4 case: max|score| is 3.6 times the cap, so cap*tanh(score/cap) materially changes the output. V is offset from zero to keep the result well-conditioned, while the softmax remains distributed rather than collapsing to one hot. This makes removal or misapplication of softcap observable.

At heads=8, qSeq=32, kvSeq=16, and headDim=64, query row 5 is fully masked by a broadcast rank-4 boolean mask while every other row remains unmasked. Row 5 of y must be zero for every head because no key has probability mass.

At heads=8, qSeq=32, kvSeq=16, and headDim=64, query row 5 receives -Infinity at every key from a broadcast rank-4 additive mask while every other row receives zero. Row 5 of y must be zero for every head, exercising the zero-denominator guard.

At heads=8, qSeq=32, kvSeq=16, and headDim=64, query row 5 receives the finite value -3.402823e+38 at every key from a broadcast rank-4 additive mask. Every masked score rounds to the same finite value, so row 5 of y must equal the uniform average of its head's 16 value rows.

Logical-bool mask at the flash cluster geometry (headDim 64, qSeq 64) with the first half of the query rows fully rejected. Unlike a finite additive float mask, a rejected bool position has zero probability mass, so those rows must emit zero rather than NaN or a mean of V while the open rows are unaffected.

Composing the causal prefix with a logical-bool mask that rejects every key of the first half of the query rows leaves those flash-cluster rows no probability-bearing key at all; they must be zero, and the causal rows below them must still be right.

Locks the materialized f32 head-dimension tail at the minimum sequence boundary. On subgroup-matrix devices, D72 exercises guarded final K and output tiles; fallback tiers retain the scalar tiled implementation.
Rank-four float32 attention with 4 query heads grouped 4:1 over 1 key/value head, head width 128, a 512-token sequence, and an explicit scale of 0.125.
Cross-attention with query length 517 and key/value length 523 checks partial final query and key tiles and the resulting normalization.
Offsetting V around 1.0 keeps the 523-key average away from zero and exposes normalization errors at partial final query and key tiles.
headDim=72 is divisible by 8 but not 16, exercising the LPQ2 clustered route with SLICE=9 and one subgroupShuffleXor reduction stage.
With is_causal=1, an explicit attention mask, and headDim=64, the clustered route must restrict keys to maxKj=qIdx+1 and then apply the additive mask within that causal range.
Unmasked rank-four attention with four-aligned Q/K and a wider value head checks output normalization.
A value-head width of 300 with a rank-4 additive float32 mask checks masked softmax and value application across a large value head.
A 512-wide value head with a boolean mask and causal attention. The all-true mask leaves causal key zero visible to every row, so no row is fully masked.

Rank-four float32 attention with 2 heads, an 8-token sequence, and a large value head width of 512. The first head's boolean mask allows no key, so it must output zero rather than divide by zero or average V; the second head's rows carry the real attention result.
The 31-query, 65-key boundary geometry is the point of the case; the amplitudes keep its answer above f16's own noise so the tolerance can stay a fraction of it.
A partial 32-query tile and one-key KV tail exercise float16 GQA prefill boundaries. Offsetting V around 1.0 makes boundary-row normalization errors observable.

One cached token and one new one, with q aligned to the cached key and orthogonal to the new one, so the two attention weights are unequal and y is a specific mixture of the two values rather than their mean. present_key/present_value are pinned to the join itself.
Two cached tokens precede a two-query block, so query i attends through key past_sequence_length+i. Zero logits make the expected rows exact means: [1,3,8] -> 4 and [1,3,8,12] -> 6.

Causal float16 attention over a 2-token cache-extended sequence with a boolean mask. Row 0 allows cached value 2 and current value 10 (mean 6); row 1 allows cached value 4 and both current values 10 and 16 (mean 10), matching the exact expected output.
Float16 counterpart of rank4_past_key_value_cache. It witnesses every optional cache port on the standard float16 T route and pins the key/value joins to directly representable values.
A logical mask over the joined past_key/K cache rejects the cached token and allows only the new token, and the mask's key-sequence dimension covers past_key followed by K rather than K alone.
With paired past inputs and only present_key requested, Y must still use past and current values, while present_value remains absent.

Only present_value is requested from a paired past cache. The bool mask rejects the cached token, so Y pins that the hidden key join still feeds attention while present_value exposes the complete value join.
Paired float16 past inputs contribute to Y even when neither optional present output is requested; Y remains float16.
Both optional present outputs are requested without past inputs. They must be exact copies of the current K and V tensors, and Y must still be computed from those direct inputs.

Only present_key is requested, with no past cache. An all-false boolean mask makes Y zero, while the requested present_key output still copies K exactly, separating cache output from the attention result.
Only present_value is requested without a past cache. This exercises the positional output hole and requires an exact V copy while Y is computed normally.
Only present_value is requested, while Y must still attend over both past and current keys.

The boolean mask allows only the cached token, and present_value is not requested. Y depends on the hidden past_value join, while the requested present_key output independently verifies the past_key/K join.
Neither present_key nor present_value is requested. A boolean mask that allows only the new token verifies Y over the joined past and current sequence.
Pins the zero-denominator rule for the masked rank-4 cache route while both joined caches remain public outputs.
A fully masked row must produce zero Y while the requested present_key remains correct.
A fully masked row must produce zero Y while the requested present_value remains correct.
A fully masked row must produce zero Y even when neither optional present cache output is requested.
Both present outputs are requested with no past cache on the masked route. An all-false row makes Y zero while both exact current-cache copies remain observable.
Unmasked no-past route with only present_key requested. The cache copy is exact and the direct K/V attention result remains independently checked.
Masked no-past route with only present_value requested. The all-false row must not suppress the exact V cache copy even though it makes Y zero.
With batch 2, four query heads over two KV heads, three cached tokens, and two new tokens, each query-head group must share the same independently joined five-token cache.
A float32 noncausal attention head of width 256 checks a large head dimension over the same outputs on every feature tier.
For a masked short prompt, head size 80 is a multiple of four but not 32, leaving the one-query-row-per-workgroup masked flash path on tiers without a fixed subgroup width.
A 32-wide value head with a different QK head width checks unmasked attention across mismatched head dimensions.
A rank-4 additive mask with a value head wider than the query/key head checks masked attention over mismatched head widths.

Rank-four float32 attention, 1 head, 4-token sequence, value head width 32. An additive mask gives query row 1 negative infinity at every key while rows 0, 2 and 3 stay finite, so row 1 of Y must be zero and the remaining rows keep their finite result.
Rank-four float32 attention with 2 query heads over 1 key/value head, head width 64: a 100-token query against a 4096-token key/value cache, with query length not a multiple of any small tile.
At query length 100, key/value length 4,096, and head width 64, offsetting V around 1.0 exposes errors in the maximum and denominator across long key ranges.

Clustered split-KV prefill at headDim=128 uses the wide LPQ8 geometry without subgroups. Zero-mean V makes relative-weight and eight-term lane-fold errors observable, with tolerance scaled to the approximately 1e-4 output magnitude.

Covers the wide LPQ8 no-subgroup split-KV geometry at headDim 128, with GQA 2:1 heads and a query-tail tile. V oscillates about 1.0 so the 4096-key average remains O(1), making errors in the softmax denominator, cross-slice partial fold, or relative lane weights visible within the f32 tolerance.
HeadDim=80 is divisible by 16 but not 32, selecting the LPQ4 no-subgroup split-KV cluster geometry and exercising its reduction and padding behavior.
Rank-four float32 attention with 6 query heads grouped 2:1 over 3 key/value heads, head width 64: a 241-token query (not a multiple of 16) against a 4096-token key/value cache.
Batch 8 x sequence 128 x 2 heads models many independent windowed attention blocks and exercises rank-4 indexing with substantial batch depth.
Batch 4 x sequence 128 x 2 heads exercises windowed rank-4 attention and batch-dependent tile indexing.

A 522x522 score matrix is not divisible by the 64-wide subgroup-matrix tile on either axis. The 8x8 interior tiles publish through collectives, while the final row, column, and corner tiles use the guarded scratch epilogue.

Rank-four float32 attention with 2 heads (no grouping), head width 64, and a 522-token sequence that is not a multiple of 64. V is offset near 1.0 so the 522-key average stays well-conditioned, exposing a missing or duplicated denominator.
Query length 517 and key length 523 exercise partial final query and key tiles. Nonzero value offsets expose omitted tail weights or incorrect normalization.
Rank-four attention with GQA 2:1, query length 513, key/value length 515, and head width 64 checks partial final query/key tiles. V is offset near 1.0 so normalization errors remain observable.

ONNX scale has no schema default literal: omission means 1/sqrt(head_size), while an explicitly supplied zero is a valid multiplier. Zero logits make both keys equally likely, so Y must be the exact average of their values.

kv longer than q under is_causal pins the UPPER-LEFT alignment: keys past the query length are never attended, which distinguishes this contract from the right-aligned cached routes.
Head dimension 128 with two query heads per KV head, 517 queries and 523 keys exercises both sequence tails. Value offset 1.0 exposes lost normalization or tail weights at strict float32 tolerances.
